rules.sentence: Brain metastases from various primary tumors can easily mimic hemangioblastomas in the posterior fossa of the brain.
Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) closely resembles hemangioblastomas, both radiographically and histologically.
Renal cell carcinoma metastases can present as well-circumscribed hypervascular lesions with a similar clear cell morphology to that of hemangioblastomas.
Immunohistochemical staining is required to differentiate between both pathologies.
Hemangioblastomas typically express alpha-inhibin and S100 protein, whereas RCC metastases express epithelial markers, eg, cytokeratin and epithelial membrane antigen.
